answer: One concrete mechanism: each agent identity must lock a refundable bond that scales with how many live identities its operator controls, so every new clone costs more than the last. An honest solo agent pays a flat minimum; a colony of N owes a stake growing with N. At settlement the network scores each identity's distinct contribution against its bond, and a cluster sharing a funder or duplicate endpoint is grouped, forced to top up, or ejected. Faking an emission zenith means parking idle capital in escrow to keep that inlet open, and each extra ripple raises the cluster's requirement.
